questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of an ASIP as presented in the context?

options.A: To provide a general‑purpose CPU that requires external memory.
options.B: To integrate CPU, memory, and I/O on a single chip for low‑cost applications.
options.C: To be optimized for a particular application or domain, such as networking.
options.D: To serve as a digital signal processor for audio and video processing.

questions.explanation:
The text states that ASIPs are “Optimized for a particular application or domain” and gives network processors as an example [Page 40].

options.B: An ASIP is a domain‑specific processor, whereas an MPU is a CPU‑only component that needs external memory.

options.D: An ASIP operates at lower clock speeds than an MPU.

options.A: Because ASIPs always consume less power than MCUs.

options.C: Because ASIPs provide hardware that is tailored to the target domain, improving efficiency.
